children: By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M
Indian shares edged higher on Wednesday as oil prices fell for a sixth straight session, though Middle East uncertainty and selling at higher levels capped gains.
The Nifty 50
rose 0.24% to 23,382.25, while the BSE Sensex
gained 0.25% to 74,709.11 as of 10:01 a.m. IST.
Fourteen of 16 major sectors rose. Small-caps
gained 0.7% and mid-caps
added 0.4%.
Asian shares headed for a sixth straight session of gains as continued demand for AI applications lifted technology stocks.[MKTS/GLOB]

Foreign investors continued to shun Indian equities, with provisional data showing net sales of 38.1 billion rupees ($398.58 million) on Tuesday, marking their eighth selling session in the last nine trading days.
Brent crude

fell 1.1% to $98.2 a barrel, dropping for the sixth straight session, as Saudi Arabia began restoring crude supply on a critical pipeline to the Red Sea and on hopes for a diplomatic solution to the US-Iran war through talks at the UN in New York.
"Falling crude prices and softer global bond yields offered a more supportive backdrop, but renewed selling at higher levels is capping the recovery," said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money.
Metal index
gained 1.2%, tracking a rise in metal prices aided by strong demand in top consumer China.
Among stocks, Arvind Smartspaces
jumped 11% after announcing the booking of over 5 billion rupees in a premium residential project in Bengaluru, Arvind Sylva.
Clean Max Enviro Energy
gained 4% after Macquarie initiated coverage with "outperform" and projected an implied upside of 26.3%, citing a steady earnings outlook.
Bajaj Finance
gained 2.2% after UBS upgraded the non-bank lender to "neutral" from "sell" and raised price target, projecting cyclical earnings upgrades.
